name: 波克朗加莱主塔
subject: 现存主祠塔与入口、台基
author: Ms Sarah Welch

references.author: Ms Sarah Welch
references.description:
The Tháp Pô Klông-Garai is a 13th century Cham Hindu temples complex built on Trau Hill about 8 kilometers from Phan Rang city center in Ninh Thuan province. It is one of the best preserved Champa monument in southern Vietnam. It is also notable for the Kate festival of Cham people every year (seventh month of the Champa calendar), one marked by Cham cultural and Siva dances, music and community events over three days. The festival prayers at the temple seek "well being of all living beings".
The complex consists of three Champa towers, the site attributed to Jaya Simhavarman III who ruled from 1285 and 1307 CE. He built it to remember the Champa king Po Klong Garai (Jaya Indravarman) who was born in a herdsman family and rose to become the first king of the historic Panduranga province (1167–1205).
Archaeological studies suggest that the site had five structures similar to Po Nagar site, but only three survive. These reflect the Thap Mam style, one of seven styles of Hindu architecture found in Vietnam. The main tower is over 20 meter high. It has three talas (storeys). The niches on all four sides and different talas feature Hindu deities. The temple opens east and the east face of the temple is dedicated to Shiva (Nataraja). Inside is the sanctum with a mukhalinga and a relief of king Po Klong Garai. The entrance is made of stone. The walls are inscribed. The second tower is about 9 meters high and sometimes called the Cong Tower (gate tower). It is architecturally equivalent to gopura (gateway) of Hindu temples separating the sacred temple space from the secular space. The third structure is sometimes called the Lua Tower (fire tower). It has a barrel or saddle-shape (9.3 m x 8.2 m x 5 m), similar to Vallabhi style architecture.

The Thap Po Klong Garai is one of many Cham Hindu temples documented by colonial era archaeologists led by Henri Parmentier.

structure_checkpoints: Portrait 1024x1536. Draw ONLY the largest MAIN SANCTUARY TOWER of Po Klong Garai, the tall tower on the LEFT in Image 2, whose solid brick mass, offset wall pilasters and heavily receding tower crown distinguish it from the smaller gate tower and the long saddle-roof FIRE building on the RIGHT. Omit the entire fire building at right and all enclosure walls in front of the main tower so its base is visible. Image 3 is a CLOSEUP of this same MAIN shrine, showing its entrance porch, grey stone lintel with dancing Shiva and tall brick relief pilasters; its cropped roof and ground must NOT crop the full tower. Preserve the full tower crown, body, entrance porch and directly supporting low plinth/entry steps. Do not draw the separately photographed small narrow-through-opening gate tower. Do not invent a taller Chinese pagoda or stone multi-tier temple. Remove trees, lamps, people and surrounding buildings.
material_observations: 暖红褐砖、局部灰褐石门框、深暗门洞；实拍色温较暖，设色避免照搬夸张橙黄饱和度。
source_note: 依据所列实拍进行艺术简化；范围为现存主祠塔与入口、台基，遮挡关系保留，不据此宣称测绘精度。原型待用户人眼验收。
prompt:
Use case: precise-object-edit / architectural atlas plate coloring.
Make ONE standalone colored companion plate for the existing heritage atlas drawing.

INPUT ROLES: Image 1 is the LINE DRAWING TO COLOR and is the exact composition/geometry master. It may have a transparent background; any white or dark backdrop in a legacy reference is not part of the subject. Following photo(s) show the actual monument or sculpture TODAY, and determine material colors only. The LAST image is a COLORED STYLE SAMPLE: borrow its refined thin contour drawing, matte mineral-pigment color areas, modest shading and subtle grain, NEVER its palette, architecture, background, or golden cast.

LOCK THE DRAWING: preserve Image 1's silhouette, position, scale, canvas aspect ratio, all storeys/eaves/bays, openings, proportions, perspective, broken parts and selected details. Color the existing drawing; do not substitute another building from the photo, change viewpoints, zoom, reconstruct missing parts, or add a backdrop scene. All original margins remain. Preserve the exact set of depicted structures or figures.

COLOR THE PRESENT REAL OBJECT: use the photographed material colors and their actual distribution under ordinary daylight or neutral indoor light. Separate aged wood, paint remnants, masonry, stone, roof tiles, present glazed tiles and present sculpture pigments. Keep actual existing polychromy or gold only where the photographed object has it. No automatic dynasty color overlay, sepia filter, gold highlights, shiny model surface, invented historical restoration, or uniformly freshly painted finish. A restrained illustrated translation of the present object, not photorealism.

STYLE: elegant fine engraved contours with gently filled semi-flat color planes, matte mineral-gouache feel, small amounts of pigment grain, at most two or three soft shadow values. The linework stays legible. Thin dark material-related contour lines, not heavy cartoon outlines. Enough substance to reward a check-in, without extravagant saturation or illumination. No dense uniform fake damage, oil-paint texture, sky, trees, people, fixtures outside the source drawing, ground shadow, labels, watermark, calligraphy, UI, border, or before/after layout. Keep blank plaques blank and do not copy text from photos.

BACKGROUND: use a perfectly flat, opaque PURE WHITE (#FFFFFF) background. The entire exterior canvas and real open-air gaps between chains, ornaments or structures are pure white. Preserve the actual material colors of the subject, including pale stone and dark door recesses; define the silhouette with clear thin contours. No paper texture, grey backdrop, gradient, checkerboard, halo, vignette, glow or ground shadow. Ignore reference backgrounds. Retain the original canvas and complete composition. A local script will remove the white background after generation.
